source: NCERT Class XI, Indian Economic Development, Ch. 3 (Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal).

sections.heading: 1. Background — The 1991 Crisis
points: By 1991 India faced a severe **economic (balance of payments) crisis**: huge fiscal deficit, low foreign exchange reserves (weeks of imports), high inflation, and heavy debt.
India approached the **IMF and World Bank** for loans, which came with conditions of **structural reform**.
This led to the **New Economic Policy (NEP), 1991** — the **LPG reforms**.

sections.heading: 2. Liberalisation
points: **Liberalisation** = removing government restrictions/controls on the economy.

Measures: **abolition of industrial licensing** (except a few), removing restrictions on private investment, **financial sector reforms** (RBI), **tax reforms**, and **trade & investment liberalisation** (lower tariffs, freer imports/exports, FDI).

sections.heading: 3. Privatisation and Globalisation
points: **Privatisation** = giving a greater role to the private sector and reducing the role of the public sector — via **disinvestment** (selling shares of PSUs) and better management (navratnas).
**Globalisation** = integrating the Indian economy with the world economy (trade, capital, technology, labour flows).
India joined the **World Trade Organisation (WTO, 1995)** and reduced trade barriers.
**Outsourcing** — a major outcome; India became a hub for IT/BPO services.

sections.heading: 4. Appraisal — Gains and Criticisms
points: **Gains:** higher **GDP growth**, growth of the **service sector (IT)**, rise in foreign investment and reserves, more consumer choice, controlled inflation.
**Criticisms:** **jobless growth**, neglect of **agriculture**, **rising inequality**, uneven benefits, and pressures on small/domestic producers.
Debate continues on whether reforms benefited all sections.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: 1991 crisis (balance of payments) → New Economic Policy (LPG reforms).
Liberalisation = removing controls (abolished industrial licensing).
Privatisation = disinvestment / greater private role.
Globalisation = integration with world economy; WTO joined 1995; outsourcing (IT/BPO).
Gains: growth + IT boom; Criticisms: jobless growth, agriculture neglected, inequality.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **1991 crisis** was a **balance of payments** crisis (foreign exchange shortage).
**Liberalisation = removing controls; Privatisation = disinvestment; Globalisation = world integration.**
India joined the **WTO in 1995**.
A key criticism of reforms is **jobless growth** and **neglect of agriculture**.
